messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: p95 inference latency breached in eu-west cluster (eu-west1). p95=850ms (SLO=300ms). started ~2026-11-05T14:18:19Z. incident created INC-4821. auto-page sent to oncall.

sre-tilly: ack — I'm on it, paging the team. digging into queue depth and node metrics.

eng-kate: quick heads-up: KV cache miss rate in eu-west jumped ~4x over baseline for long-tail sequences, also seeing higher dispatch latency in the shard dispatcher logs.

ops-martin: autoscaler show: min-nodes=4, current=4, pending pods waiting for GPUs due to allocation quota. looks like we hit a spotty placement issue.

sre-tilly: customer impact summary: standard/free traffic in EU showing high latency and timeouts. gold/reserved customers still routed to dedicated pool — their latency looks OK. cs-elaine: any inbound CS tickets?

cs-elaine: got 2 pings: AcmeBank (gold) reporting slow completions — asked for traces. Note: both are hitting eu-west but show fallbacks to eu-central sometimes. also NoteChat (free) thread complaining about token churn. I'm triaging.

pm-aaron: proposal: immediate live mitigation: 1) apply per-tier steering so gold stays on eu-west-dedicated, 2) shift standard/free -> eu-central primary with us-west as fallback; 3) temporarily reduce standard tier weight in eu-west by 40%; 4) disable experimental streaming for free tier to reduce outlier long-seq load. this buys us time while infra recovers.

eng-kate: +1. Also recommend a temporary per-tier per-region rate cap (soft) to avoid cascade while we scale. cap standard: 60% throughput in eu-west. remainder gets routed to eu-central.

sre-tilly: executing mitigation now. patching smart-routing policy and applying a temporary ratecap. will post the exact change.

sre-tilly: ```json
{
  "policy_id": "smart-routing-v2",
  "changes": [
    {
      "match": { "tier": "gold" },
      "route": [{ "region": "eu-west", "weight": 100, "pool": "reserved" }]
    },
    {
      "match": { "tier": ["standard","free"] },
      "route": [
        { "region": "eu-central", "weight": 60 },
        { "region": "eu-west", "weight": 40 },
        { "region": "us-west", "weight": 0, "fallback": true }
      ],
      "overrides": { "streaming": false }
    }
  ],
  "meta": { "reason": "live mitigation for eu-west latency spike", "author": "sre-tilly", "expires_in": "2h" }
}
```

sre-tilly: applying via control plane: `rictl routing apply --policy smart-routing-v2 --patch-file /tmp/temp-mitigation.json --force`

incident-bot: mitigation request submitted (req_id=mit-20261105-73). routing change propagated to control plane, waiting for edge sync.

ops-martin: edge sync completed for routing table, CDN/edge decisions updated. pushing per-tier token throttle for eu-west: `redis-cli -h ratecache set tier:standard:eu-west:cap 0.6` — verified.

eng-kate: checks: eu-west queue depth dropping from 1.8k -> 900 within 3 minutes. KV miss rate still slightly high but trending down. p95 latency improved to ~420ms (still above SLO but better).

cs-elaine: notified affected customers: AcmeBank + NoteChat + two smaller dev teams. Message template sent: 
"We're seeing elevated latency in eu-west, mitigation activated: lower-priority traffic is being routed to eu-central. Gold/reserved traffic preserved. We'll post updates as we stabilize."

pm-aaron: good. can we watch the cost impact? rerouting to eu-central could increase egress/costs and higher token rate on eu-central pools. Set a watch, flag finance if >10% cost burn.

eng-kate: enabling extra batching on eu-central to reduce per-token cost; but fewer caches there so latency might bump up. tradeoff accepted for now.

sre-tilly: monitoring dashboard snapshots: 
- eu-west p95: 420ms -> trending down
- eu-central p95: 520ms (for newly routed standard traffic)
- error rate: unchanged
- queue depth eu-west: 900 -> 600

ops-martin: note: we also hit a placement anomaly in eu-west that prevented adding new GPUs fast. raising support ticket with infra quota team, but mitigation buys us a buffer.

eng-kate: extra safety: add a canary rule so if eu-central p95 > 800ms we throttle route back to eu-west and auto-fallback to us-west. want to avoid oscillation.

sre-tilly: adding canary guard in policy: will add `circuit-breaker` for region target. patching.

sre-tilly: ```yaml
- name: cb-eu-central-p95
  target: eu-central
  metric: p95
  threshold_ms: 800
  action: reduce-weight-by: 50
  cooldown: 300s
```

incident-bot: circuit-breaker rule applied (cb-id=cb-20261105-3).

eng-kate: monitoring logs for long-tail seqs and model mismatch. if the rollout of quantized 1.2 is causal we'll roll it back from canaries in eu-west-only.

sre-tilly: canary rollback queued: `rictl model rollback --model quant-1.2 --region eu-west --selector canary=true` — executing after current mitigation confirms stability.

cs-elaine: update for customers: AcmeBank prefers EU-only, offered option to route to dedicated EU-central reserved pool as temporary. they accepted.

pm-aaron: next steps: 1) keep mitigation for 2 hours, 2) escalate infra placement if not resolved, 3) postmortem after incident close. assign owners.

sre-tilly: I'm handing off monitoring and follow-ups to @oncall-next in 25m. leaving a runbook note: what I changed, request ids, and customer contacts in the incident doc.

oncall-next: ack — taking ownership. I'll watch the dashboards and escalate to infra if placement doesn't free up. please ping me if any policy rollbacks or customer impacts change.

cs-elaine: I'll continue customer comms and collect any new reports.

eng-kate: I'll hold on the model rollback until oncall confirms p95 stable.

ops-martin: infra ticket submitted: TT-90521 for GPU allocation anomaly. linking here.

sre-tilly: final note before stepping off: mitigation applied, initial improvement observed. estimated time to stable ~30-60m if placement finishes. handoff to @oncall-next. :white_check_mark:

oncall-next: thanks — I'll update INC-4821 and post timeline. taking over. :thumbsup:
